title: Keep the head and the tail

holes.prompt: What happens when the caller asks for a very small budget?

options.why: No floor. A caller that passes 12 gets eight bytes of head and four of tail, which is not an excerpt of anything — and the elision marker is longer than the text it replaced.
A floor, so the result is always big enough to be worth reading. 256 is not magic; it is 'longer than the elision marker, with a line or two either side'.

holes.prompt: How much of the output do you keep, and from where?

options.why: The obvious one, and the one almost every harness ships. It is also the one that loses the line you needed: a failing test run puts the summary at the end, and a panic puts the error there too.
Two thirds head, one third tail. The head carries what the command was doing; the tail carries how it ended. The middle is the part a model can most often do without.
Keeps the outcome and throws away the command that produced it. Better than head-only for a test run, worse for anything that fails early.

holes.prompt: The cut lands in the middle of a multi-byte character. Then what?

options.why: Cut anyway. The output ends in half a rune, which prints as a replacement character — and if the model quotes it back, the broken byte travels into the next request.
Walk back to a rune boundary. Costs at most three bytes and means the excerpt is always valid UTF-8, which everything downstream assumes.

hints: Run it with head-only selected and read the last line of the output you get.
What does `go test` print last, and where would it be after a head-only cut?
